etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin comicus, from Ancient Greek κωμικός (kōmikós, “relating to comedy”), from κῶμος (kômos, “carousal”).

definitions.definition: Pertaining to comedy, as a literary genre. [from 16th c.]
Using the techniques of comedy, as a composition, performer etc; amusing, entertaining. [from 16th c.]

quote.citation: 1954, Canadian Saturday Night: A Magazine of Business & National Affairs:
quote.text: There is a quartet of comic musicians, who perform on instruments of an inconceivable bassness  […]

quote.citation: 1792, Charlotte Smith, Desmond, Broadview, published 2001, page 262:
quote.text: As there was something excessively comique in the distress of the landlord and his wife  […] , I could not forbear staying a little to be amused with it.

definitions.definition: A story composed of drawn images arranged in  a sequence, usually with textual captions; a graphic novel.
